thread:
nina: Heads-up: I'm collecting feedback on prefetch semantics + fallback behavior for paginated endpoints. We need a single, cross-SDK pattern that balances user ergonomics, infra load, and clear failure modes.

leo: TL;DR: expose prefetch mode + limits, make prefetch best-effort, and require explicit opt-in for any fallback that changes error semantics.

nina: Quick set of user-facing opts I propose: prefetch: none|adjacent|buffered, prefetch_pages: int, prefetch_bytes: int, fallback: none|stream|list_all (opt-in).

raj: Agree. Important: fallback->list_all can cause large memory usage and hidden costs. Should only be allowed when server advertises supports_unary_list and client sets an explicit max_items guard.

zoe: Language ergonomics notes: Python iterators can hide prefetch behind the iterator API easily. TS async iterators likewise. Go needs an explicit iterator type with Close()/Cancel() so prefetch goroutines can be stopped.

leo: Operationally we need a server capability schema: {supports_streaming: bool, supports_unary_list: bool, max_page_size: int}. SDKs consult this at init or route binding.

nina: Failure modes: if a prefetched page fails, do NOT surface to caller immediately. Prefetch failures are logged and counted. Only surface error if current page is affected or fallback_to_stream is enabled and kicks in.

raj: On retries: prefetch should use separate retry budget and shorter deadline (e.g., 300ms) than the primary request. Prefetch must not consume the primary retry attempts. If prefetch triggers fallback, the fallback operation should be treated as a separate user-visible attempt (with request-id and server dedupe recommended).

zoe: Cancellation example for Go:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
it := client.ListWidgets(ctx, ListOpts{PageSize:50, Prefetch:"adjacent", PrefetchPages:1, Fallback:"stream"})
defer it.Close()
for it.Next() {
  w := it.Value()
  handle(w)
  if shouldStop(w) { cancel(); break }
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Error(err) }
```

leo: Telemetry: counters -> prefetch_attempts, prefetch_success, prefetch_failures, fallback_invoked, fallback_path. Traces should link prefetch requests to the parent call via span_id.

nina: Security/economics: Hosted tier default must be conservative to avoid accidental load/cost spikes. Proposal: Hosted default = prefetch:none, Dedicated/Private default = prefetch:adjacent (unless admin overrides).

raj: Backpressure: expose max_prefetch_concurrency and honor server-side quotas. Client should back off prefetch aggressively when it sees rate-limit 429s to avoid herd behavior.

zoe: Edge-case: if the first page returns a resume token but no items, adjacent prefetch should still fetch next page to avoid an extra wait cycle. Document this behavior.

leo: API surface samples — TypeScript:```ts
const pages = client.listWidgets({ pageSize: 40, prefetch: 'adjacent', prefetchPages: 1, fallback: 'stream' })
for await (const page of pages) { for (const w of page.items) handle(w) }
```

Python:```py
for page in client.list_widgets(page_size=40, prefetch='adjacent', prefetch_pages=1, fallback='stream'):
    for w in page.items:
        handle(w)
```

nina: Implementation plan:
1) Server: add capability flags in route metadata - raj
2) Transport: add background-request plumbing and separate retry budget - leo
3) SDKs: unify surface and add cancel/close hooks - zoe
4) Docs/optimize integration: add telemetry hooks and migration doc - nina

raj: I'll draft a small compatibility matrix showing what each language will default to and how to opt-in. Also will add recommendations for request-id header so servers can dedupe fallback attempts.

zoe: I'll prototype the Go iterator (cancel + prefetch stop) and push sample benchmarks.

nina: Ok. If no blockers by EOD we'll turn this into an RFC with concrete code samples and a note on costs. :thumbsup:
